Based on the CCC Crash Course 2026 report, here are the key findings regarding average repair cost growth and repairable claims trends:

## Average Repair Cost Growth

The average total cost of repair (TCOR) reached $4,818 for 2025, a 1.7% increase over 2024, which is notably the lowest rate of increase since 2017. This represents a significant slowdown compared to prior years. Compared to 2020, when the average repairable vehicle appraisal was $3,421, the 2025 average total repair cost of $4,818 represents an increase of about 40.8% in five years.

## Repairable Claims Trends

Repairable claim volume declined 9.7% in 2025 across all coverages. However, the composition of these claims has shifted significantly. The share of repairable collision claims for vehicles six years old or newer fell to 58.3% in 2025, down from over 67% in 2020.

## Key Complexity Driver: Calibrations

28.3% of repairable estimates now include calibrations, reflecting increasing vehicle technology complexity. In Q4 2025, 28.3% of all repairable estimates included at least one sensor calibration, up from 21.8% in Q4 2024, with each calibration adding $350 to $500 to the repair bill.

## Valuation Multiples

For 2026, collision repair businesses are valued with 4x-8x EBITDA multiples when acquired by named MSO buyers. However, multiples vary significantly by scale: 3x to 5x SDE for single-shop owner-operators, 4x to 6x EBITDA for managed single shops, 6x to 9x for multi-shop operators with 3 to 10 locations, and 8x to 12x for platform-grade MSOs.

Verified active 2026 buyers include Caliber Collision (Hellman & Friedman / Leonard Green / OMERS), Crash Champions (Clearlake Capital), Classic Collision (TPG Capital), Boyd Group / Gerber Collision (TSX: BYD), Quality Collision Group (Susquehanna Private Capital), and the Driven Brands collision franchise group.

Caliber Collision, Boyd Group's Gerber Collision, Crash Champions, Joe Hudson's, Classic Collision, and Quality Collision Group dominate add-on bidding above $1.5M EBITDA.

## EBITDA Multiples

Market multiples remained relatively stable at approximately 7x EBITDA throughout 2025, despite significant market headwinds. Declining revenue and lower EBITDA reduced enterprise values even though valuation multiples remained relatively stable.

Collision repair merger and acquisition activity dropped significantly in 2025, with fewer deals, longer timelines and lower valuations driven by declining claim counts and revenue pressure. Three new PE firms entered the sector during 2025, joining the existing roster of 14 PE investors seeking exposure to the industry's defensive characteristics and consolidation opportunities. Focus Advisors expects at least three additional PE entrants in 2026.

PE firms that historically pursued established MSOs with $30 million or more in revenue moved downstream in 2025, pursuing operators with as few as one to three locations.

## Notable Deal

In early November, a blockbuster event — Boyd Group/Gerber announced its merger with Joe Hudson's Collision Centers, which was described as exceptional in an otherwise slow year for M&A.
